threads.body:
[API] `MessagingExceptionEventExtractors` is in a public semconv package but depends on `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.api.internal.Experimental` (an explicitly internal/temporary bridge API). This effectively exposes internal wiring as part of the incubator public surface area, which makes it harder to evolve/remove when a stable `InstrumenterBuilder` API for exception-log configuration is introduced.

Consider moving this helper into an `.internal` package (similar to `...builder.internal.DefaultHttp*InstrumenterBuilder`), or otherwise keeping the internal dependency from leaking into the public semconv namespace (e.g., introduce a public builder method once available and delegate to that).

replies.body: Addressed — moved all five exception-event helpers into their `semconv.{domain}.internal` subpackages so the public incubator surface no longer depends on the internal `Experimental` bridge API (following the existing HTTP precedent, which keeps this wiring inside `.internal`). Updated all caller imports accordingly.

threads.body: `testExceptionSignalLogs` doesn't inherit the same `testLatestDeps` / `collectMetadata` system properties as the main `test` task. If those flags are enabled in CI or local runs, this task will execute `WrapperTest` under a different configuration than the rest of the suite, and metadata collection may be skipped for this run.

replies.body: Fixed. The Kafka clients 2.6 library now configures the shared Test-task settings via `withType<Test>().configureEach`, so both `test` and `testExceptionSignalLogs` use the Testcontainers build service and receive `testLatestDeps` and `collectMetadata`. The preview task keeps its logs-mode flag and now also sets `metadataConfig=otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` for metadata collection.

threads.body: `emitExceptionAsLogs()` is computed once in `SemconvExceptionSignal` during class initialization (based on the JVM/system properties and GlobalOpenTelemetry config). This test never sets `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` for the test JVM, so on a normal test run `emitExceptionAsLogs()` will almost always be false and these tests will only assert that no logs were emitted, without ever validating the configured event names/severities/attributes for the logs path.

replies.body: No code change needed. The current PR head already wires `testExceptionSignalLogs` with `-Dotel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs` and `testExceptionSignalLogsDup` with `logs/dup`; both tasks run the normal test classes/runtime classpath, and `check` depends on both tasks.

threads.body: [Testing] In logs mode (`otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs`), this test currently stops asserting anything about span exceptions, so it would still pass even if the exception continued to be emitted as a span event (regressing the intended behavior). Use the existing `hasException(... ? error : null)` pattern to also assert *absence* of span exceptions when span events are disabled.
